reader.notes: MEAN is the SDIDI quotient in every mode (IntrinsicCarrierRules.SdidiQuotientFunctions, MeanDec), so the 19-digit sum of two 18-digit maxima does not overflow. EF printing 3.99999999 for MEAN(2 1 1)*3 is the truncated quotient carried into the product; the returned value's precision is implementor-defined (§1989:A.2.3 GR2). Every probe prints the same at --std 2023.

refuter.evidence: meanctx2-001 at --std 85: C1 COMPUTE PIC 9 = MEAN (1 2) * 2 gives 3 (MEAN's scale is not the receiver's), C2 ROUNDED MEAN (1 2) 2, C3 ROUNDED MEAN (0 1 1) 1, C6 IF MEAN (1 2) = 1.5 true (receiverless context), CC MEAN (TE (ALL)) of 1.5 -2.5 0.5 9.9 = 2.35, CE MEAN (TQE (ALL 3) TQE (2 ALL)) = 7.2, CF MEAN of eleven 18-digit maxima = K, C9 MEAN (FUNCTION MEDIAN (1 2) 1) = 1.25, CI MEAN (FUNCTION INTEGER (2.5) 4) = 3; degen-001 G3 MEAN (W-N) = -1.25. numplace-001: MOVE FUNCTION MEAN (1 2) TO R2 refused COBOL0900 at 85 (§1989:A.2.3 GR2 'A numeric function may be used only in an arithmetic expression'), accepted at 2023. Attack tried and not decisive: meanprec2-001 P1 COMPUTE PIC 9(18) = MEAN (K F) with K = 999999999999999999 and F = .999999999999999999 stores 500000000000000000 and P5 IF MEAN (K F) < 500000000000000000 is false, while the exact mean is 499999999999999999.9999999999999999995 (MEDIAN (K F), the same mean by RV2 of MEDIAN, gives 499999999999999999, P2/P6): the exact quotient is rounded once to 34 digits. The 1985 text gives that to the implementor (cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.4 'The implementor specifies the representation of integer and numeric functions'; OK §1985:IV.4.3.4 'Each implementor will indicate the techniques used in evaluating integer and numeric functions') and docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-123.md documents the 34-digit rounding of MEAN; identical at --std 2023 (meanprec2-002). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.24.4 RV1 'the arithmetic mean of the argument-1 series'.
